feedback.problem:
If $\,T\,$ is a linear transformation and $\,T([\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -20\end{aligned}]$, then find $T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]).$

| $\,T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}])=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation, it must satisfy $T(kv)=kT(v).$ Noting that $[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}]=2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T([\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}]) & =T(2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}])=2T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since we're told that 

$$
T([\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -20\end{aligned}],
$$

we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}2T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
